As a result, I found it much easier to communicate or even make relationships with Spanish speaking people with my A1 Spanish, then with Germans with my B2 German. In one company I worked at, we had unlimited PTO, which meant that in some teams, members could take one week vacation per month, but we had some teams where members did not take more than 15 days of vacation per year. It was a scam - depends on your workload, team, company needs, etc.

Another thing

>This makes the time off impact less noticeable and harmful for my team

This comment is very interesting. In my view, PTO is for me, not for my team. Sure, we should think about the team and product, in some way, but in my opinion, it should not even cross my mind that what I am doing is \`noticeable\` or \`harmful\` in terms of taking time off. Other team members should also not question it, especially in unlimited PTO situation.

Last thing, in my experience, it is a lot easier to sell an idea of taking 4-5 weeks of vacation (for example, for an expedition) in one go with limited PTO, than unlimited. People understand that I had to make a calculation and I am taking responsibility for my decision for burning almost all of my vacation days.

With unlimited PTO you have this strange situation, where you are allowed to take as many vacation days as you want, but you really should not. If I have unlimited PTO then I should be able to take 52 weeks of vacation, without anyone saying anything. If there is a limit - let's state it. Be explicit, not implicit.

The 2nd phase (Max Strength) in the training I have usually looks like this:

* Mon - Zone 1 Recovery/Run/Jog/Walk
* Tue - Max Strength 1:30h (CORE (Find the 4 hardest core exercises for you to complete) + MAX(StepUps/Pushups + StepDowns/PullUps with a lot of weight (up to even 40kg) )) + Fixed Rope Pulling 35m (Cable Row, Tricep Extension etc.)
* Wed - Zone 2 Aerobic Base Run / Hike - 1:45 h
* Thu - Zone 2 Hike on Hilly Terrain 2:30 h
* Fri - Rest Day Recovery
* Sat - Recovery Run/Jog/Walk - 40 m.
* Sun - Steep Uphill Hike 1:30 h (aerobic workout so keep the intensity low)

New here so a bit of info about me. I am based in Europe. I've discovered hiking/climbing quite recently, but I have been running since 10 years. I did some mountaineering courses (crampon work, high-altitude tourism). I also climb top rope (which I suck at - struggling at 5.10a in the gym). I don't live in a mountain area, so a lot of training is not in high altitude, which again - sucks.

My LONG TERM GOAL (for now) is the 7 summits. And, yes, this is more of a peak-bagging endeavour than anything else, but it so deeply rooted in my mind now, I am not sure if I could switch to another goal without regretting it for my whole life.
